info.name: Paw-M API — Full Collection V3
info.description:
Complete, production-grade Postman collection for the Paw-M Veterinary Clinic backend API.

Base URL  : {{baseUrl}}   (default: http://localhost:3001)
Auth model: Bearer JWT. A collection-level pre-request script auto-logs-in the three seeded staff roles (admin / payroll / staff) and stores their fresh JWTs in adminToken / staffToken / payrollToken. Every protected request already carries the correct Authorization header — you can hit Send on any request and it just works.

Seeded credentials
  admin   / admin123
  payroll / payroll123
  staff   / staff123

Client-side (storefront) flows
  Client Auth folder lets you REGISTER a store client -> read the 6-digit email code -> VERIFY (token saved) -> LOGIN. After that, /api/pets, /api/bookings (create) and /api/me run as that client via {{clientToken}}. To change the target, edit clientEmail / clientPassword.

Running order
  0..3 setup/auth -> 4/5/6 catalog (creates a QA doctor, service, product) -> 7/8/9 bookings & orders & payments -> 10 reviews -> 11 work sessions -> 12 prescriptions -> 13 pets -> 14 employees -> 15 payroll -> 16 tasks -> 17 notifications -> 18 audit logs -> 19 cookie/CSRF demo.

Cookie + CSRF (optional demo)
  The API also supports same-origin cookie sessions. Folder 19 shows the double-submit flow: login sets paw-m-session + paw-m-csrf-token cookies, and state-changing requests must echo the CSRF cookie in X-CSRF-Token. Bearer mode (used everywhere else) bypasses CSRF.

Environment switch
  Local:  baseUrl = http://localhost:3001
  Prod :  baseUrl = https://pawmclinnic.com  (or your API host; BEARER mode is recommended over HTTPS)

Samples are chained: every create request stores its id into a variable (sampleDoctorId, sampleProductId, sampleOrderId, ...) so downstream PATCH/DELETE/GET requests target the record you just created.

exec: // Collection pre-request: refresh dynamic dates + auto-login the seeded staff roles.
body: { mode: 'raw', raw: JSON.stringify({ username: pm.collectionVariables.get(userVar), password: pm.collectionVariables.get(passVar) }) }

item.name: 0 — Health & Server
GET /api/health
item.description: Liveness probe. Confirms only that the process is running; it does not touch the database. Expects 200 { status: 'ok', db: 'unchecked', uptimeSeconds }.

exec: pm.test('db not asserted by liveness', () => pm.expect(j.db).to.eql('unchecked'));

item.name: GET /api/ready
item.description: Readiness probe. Runs a real SELECT 1 under a hard timeout, so it reports whether the database is actually usable. Expects 200 { status: 'ready', db: 'connected', latencyMs }, or 503 { status: 'degraded', db: 'disconnected' }.

item.name: OPTIONS — CORS preflight
item.description: Browser preflight. Expects 204 with CORS headers.

item.name: GET /api/auth/config
item.description: True once at least one staff account exists.
Boot checks.

item.name: 1 — Auth (Staff Sessions)
POST /api/auth/login (admin)
item.description: Logs in as admin. Stores the JWT in adminToken for all later admin calls.

item.name: POST /api/auth/login (staff)
item.description: Logs in as staff (least-privilege role for POS / counter).

item.name: POST /api/auth/login (payroll)
item.description: Logs in as payroll — can read payroll records + low-stock, but not admin-only routes.

item.name: POST /api/auth/login (wrong password)
item.description: Wrong password returns { ok: false } (rate-limit after repeated attempts).

item.name: GET /api/auth/me (who am I)
item.description: Returns the current session user { authenticated, id, username, role }.

item.name: POST /api/auth/logout
item.description: Clears the session cookie. Stateless JWTs stay valid until expiry.

item.name: POST /api/auth/forgot-password
item.description: Sends a 6-digit reset code to the account email (generic response either way).

item.name: POST /api/auth/reset-password
item.description: FINISHES the reset — only works within 15 min of forgot-password. Replace code with the real one.

item.name: PUT /api/auth/credentials (rotate password)
item.description: WARNING — rotates the LIVE admin credential. This example keeps the same password/username so it is a no-op; change fields to actually rotate.

item.name: POST /api/auth/accounts (create account with role — admin)
item.description: Creates a login account with an explicit role (staff / payroll / admin). Needs adminToken. Add new admins safely — uses newAccountUsername / newAccountPassword / newAccountRole variables. Caches the new account id in sampleAccountId.

exec: if (pm.response.code === 201) { pm.collectionVariables.set('sampleAccountId', j.id); console.log('created account', j.username, 'role', j.role, 'id', j.id); }

item.name: POST /api/auth/accounts (duplicate → 409)
item.description: Re-creates the same username to prove the duplicate check. Expects 409 'Username already exists'.

item.name: GET /api/auth/accounts (list accounts — admin)
item.description: Lists all login accounts with their roles. Use this to verify the account you created (or the demo flow in Folder 1).

item.name: PATCH /api/auth/accounts/:id/role (change role — admin)
item.description: Changes the role of the account cached in sampleAccountId. Guarded: the last remaining admin can never be demoted. To run, first execute the create-account request (or set sampleAccountId manually) and set the new role in the body.
Staff JWT sessions. Pre-request auto-login keeps tokens fresh.

item.name: 2 — Client Auth & Client Portal
POST /api/client-auth/register
item.description: Requests email verification. Sends a 6-digit code — read it from the inbox, set clientVerifyCode... (see next step). 409 if email already registered.

item.name: POST /api/client-auth/verify (code from email)
item.description: Verifies the emailed code, creates the account and returns a session token (stored in clientToken). PUT THE REAL EMAILED CODE where 123456 is.

item.name: POST /api/client-auth/login
item.description: Client login for an already-verified account. Stores token in clientToken. Useful to re-auth after clearing the variable.

item.name: POST /api/client-auth/logout
item.description: Destroys the client session server-side.

item.name: GET /api/me (client profile bundle)
item.description: Client account + pets + bookings + orders + prescriptions in one call. Requires a verified clientToken.

exec: console.log(JSON.stringify({ client: j.client && j.client.email, pets: j.pets && j.pets.length, bookings: j.bookings && j.bookings.length }, null, 2));

item.description: Storefront client authentication. Register -> get code from email -> verify. Token auto-saved to clientToken.

item.name: 8 — Orders
GET /api/orders (staff list)

item.name: PATCH /api/orders/:id/status (→ completed — staff)

item.name: PATCH /api/orders/:id/archive (staff)
item.description: Soft-archive.

item.name: DELETE /api/orders/:id (cleanup — staff)

item.description: Currently open shift or null.

exec: pm.test('null or session', () => pm.expect(j === null || typeof j.id === 'string').to.be.true);

item.name: POST /api/work-session/check-out (staff)

item.name: POST /api/work-session/check-out (not checked in — 400)

item.name: GET /api/work-sessions/all (all sessions — admin)

item.name: GET /api/work-sessions/me/kpi (staff)

item.name: 19 — Session & CSRF (cookie auth demo)
POST /api/auth/login (admin cookies)
item.description: Same-origin flow: sets paw-m-session (httpOnly) + paw-m-csrf-token (readable) cookies. Stores the CSRF value so state-changing cookie-auth requests can echo it.

exec: if (!csrf && pm.response && pm.response.cookies) { const c = pm.response.cookies; for (let i = 0; i < c.length; i++) { if (c[i].name === 'paw-m-csrf-token') csrf = c[i].value; } }
pm.test('session cookie present', () => pm.cookies.get('paw-m-session') !== undefined && pm.cookies.get('paw-m-session') !== '');

item.name: PATCH /api/settings (cookie + CSRF header — WORKS)
item.description: NO Authorization header — authenticated via the session cookie. The double-submit X-CSRF-Token must match the paw-m-csrf-token cookie for state-changing methods. Expect 200.

item.name: PATCH /api/settings (cookie WITHOUT CSRF — BLOCKED)
item.description: Cookie present but X-CSRF-Token missing → 403 CSRF token mismatch. This is the protection that Bearer auth skips.

item.name: POST /api/auth/logout
item.description: Clears both cookies.
Explains the cookie + double-submit CSRF flow. Production over HTTPS uses SameSite=None+Secure cookies.
